sensor_rigs.declared_by: the policy, through scenario_orchestration/policy.py's sensors(); osc2carla/backend/sensors.py attaches exactly what it returns and invents nothing

known.simlingo: one 1024x512 fov-110 forward camera at (-1.5, 0, 2.0), the CARLA Leaderboard mounting
known.tfv6: three 384x384 fov-60 cameras at yaw -57.5/0/+57.5, one 64-channel LiDAR, four radars; the radar ORDER is part of the format

sensor_rigs.backends: carla only. The bundled local simulator provides sensor.other.collision and nothing else, so a sensor policy there is refused with a reason rather than driven against an empty rig.
sensor_rigs.synchronisation: each sensor has its own queue and a capture blocks for the measurement stamped with the tick being described, discarding anything older, so the frames and the pose a policy reasons over are one tick.

policies.external: any ego_policy_v1 policy whose repository exposes scenario_orchestration/policy.py; it is loaded through scenario_orchestration/osc2carla_policy_bridge.py

notes.identity: Independent reimplementation of the OpenSCENARIO 2.1 -> CARLA compiler of arXiv:2604.16452. Scenarios are .osc source compiled to a py_trees behaviour tree; the native id of a family is its .osc file.
notes.closed_loop: Declared true, and this disagrees with configs/algorithm/osc2runner.yaml, which declares false. The adversary timelines are compiled and open-loop, but their triggers are live monitors on the ego's state, and --ego-policy hands the ego's actuation to an external controller that is ticked once per simulated step against a fresh state observation. Only the compiled 'scripted' arm is open-loop end to end.
notes.observation_spaces: state and sensor. On the CARLA backend the state document is the full object-centric scene the harness's 'state' space defines -- ego speed, ego-frame object tokens, a 20-point ego-frame route, the posted speed limit, and a BEV semantic raster produced by the policy repository's own renderer (scenario_orchestration/bev.py) -- alongside this repository's own car-following view (pose, world-frame route, closest leader). A policy that declares its own rig through sensors() additionally receives that rig's camera, LiDAR and radar measurements for the same tick. The rig is the policy's, never this repository's: a sensorimotor model is trained behind one set of intrinsics and mountings, and a rig chosen here would publish this repository's behaviour under the model's name. On the local backends there is no CARLA world to describe, so only the car-following view is sent, an object-centric policy refuses the observation itself rather than being handed a substituted one, and a sensor policy is refused before the run starts.
notes.stop_sign: Not a family this harness defines. Declared because the repository implements it and its intended outcome is the absence of a collision, which makes it the one family here whose success does not depend on a conflict developing on schedule.
notes.scenario_parameters: implementation.parameters.town is advisory. Each .osc hard-codes the stage geometry of one map (keep(it.map_file == ...)), so on the CARLA backend the town comes from the scenario and a differing request parameter is recorded, not applied. On the local backend a request town is applied only when it names one of the bundled road networks (grid, highway, loop, two_lane, wide_grid).
notes.seed: The pipeline exposes no seed. The local simulator is deterministic (fixed step, no substepping), so repeats of one cell are bit-identical and the seed carries no information; on CARLA the variation comes from physics substepping, which no seed here controls. The requested seed is recorded with every result.
notes.trace: No per-step trace is emitted. The run summary written by osc2carla/backend/metrics.py is copied into the output directory as osc2carla_metrics.json and referenced from method_metrics. Under an external policy the summary carries ego_policy_detail, which records the rig that was attached, the rate it was sampled at, anything that failed to attach or dropped a frame, the decision count, and whatever the policy reports about itself.
notes.action_spaces: control on every backend. 'waypoints' is accepted through the 'control' block a waypoint policy's own lateral/longitudinal controllers return alongside its waypoints, so the policy's published closed-loop behaviour is reproduced rather than re-derived by a controller written here; a waypoint policy that returns no control cannot be actuated and is reported as such. 'trajectory' is not accepted.
notes.bev: carla_garage.birds_eye_view.chauffeurnet.ObsManager, imported from the policy repository rather than reimplemented. CARLA's layered builds report an _Opt suffix for which no raster ships; Town10HD.xodr and Town10HD_Opt.xodr are byte-identical in CARLA 0.9.16, so the policy repository carries Town10HD_Opt.h5 as a symlink and the substitution is recorded in the run report.
notes.ego_vehicle: The scenario chooses it, and for the six conflict families it is vehicle.tesla.model3. SimLingo's released checkpoint was trained behind the leaderboard hero vehicle.lincoln.mkz_2020 (4.89 m vs 4.79 m), so its fixed camera mount sits marginally differently relative to the body than in training. Recorded because the policy's own README calls the ego vehicle load-bearing; not corrected, because the ego model is part of the scenario, not of the runner.
notes.traffic_lights_and_a_policy_that_sees: Read every sensor-policy result against this. The scenarios express a signal phase as behaviour and geometry -- there is no action to set or read one, and scripted actors never yield to CARLA's own signals (see the header of scenarios/benchmark/red_light.osc). A camera policy has no such exemption: CARLA's lights run their default cycle and are in frame, so the ego stops for them. Measured on red_light and left_turn, simlingo reported 'Remain stopped due to the red traffic light' and travelled 17-73 m where the analytic arm travelled 97 m, and the phase it meets differs between runs of the same file. The conflict a scenario stages therefore may or may not develop, which is a property of the scenario vocabulary meeting a policy that perceives, not a defect in the rig.
notes.video: OSC2CARLA_RECORD_VIDEO writes <family>.mp4 into the output directory: a top-down view and a chase camera side by side, and beneath them -- whenever an ego policy attached a rig -- that rig's own frames beside the command the policy returned. A rig mounted wrong, pointed backwards or delivering the previous tick still produces plausible numbers and an obviously wrong video, which is what makes the band worth the pixels.
